facts.value: The concept of purebred bloodstock and a controlled, written breed registry has come to be particularly significant and important in modern times.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Sometimes purebred horses are incorrectly or inaccurately called 'thoroughbreds'.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: 'Thoroughbred' is a specific breed of horse, while a 'purebred' is a horse (or any other animal) with a defined pedigree recognized by a breed registry.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Horse breeds are groups of horses with distinctive characteristics that are transmitted consistently to their offspring, such as conformation, color, performance ability, or disposition.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: These inherited traits result from a combination of natural crosses and artificial selection methods.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Horses have been selectively bred since their domestication.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: An early example of people who practiced selective horse breeding was the Bedouin, who had a reputation for careful practices, keeping extensive pedigrees of their Arabian horses and placing great value upon pure bloodlines.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: These pedigrees were originally transmitted via an oral tradition.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Breeds developed due to a need for 'form to function', the necessity to develop certain characteristics in order to perform a particular type of work.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: A powerful but refined breed such as the Andalusian developed as riding horses with an aptitude for dressage.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Heavy draft horses were developed out of a need to perform demanding farm work and pull heavy wagons.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Other horse breeds had been developed specifically for light agricultural work, carriage and road work, various sport disciplines, or simply as pets.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Some breeds developed through centuries of crossing other breeds, while others descended from a single foundation sire or other limited or restricted foundation bloodstock.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: One of the earliest formal registries was General Stud Book for Thoroughbreds, which began in 1791 and traced back to the foundation bloodstock for the breed.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: There are more than 300 horse breeds in the world today.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick
